denominator_note: wall time and unit counts below are per-BUCKET, re-derived from the ATLAS PARTITION of core_rulebook units ONLY (python3 scripts/completion_atlas.py --book core_rulebook --check), not corpus-wide. This differs from step-cost-ledger.derived.json (an earlier, explicitly-marked-PARTIAL input authored by an orchestrator pass), which measured corpus-wide unit closure by commit shape (generic vs narrow) rather than by atlas bucket letter for one book. That file remains as a secondary cross-check; this file is the criterion's own evidence artifact.

measurement_method.wall_time: commit-to-commit timestamp span for every commit touching docs/work-inventory.json between the tranche/14 cut (ea2b3396f2) and this cycle's own HEAD, via `git log --reverse --format=%ct ea2b3396f2..HEAD -- docs/work-inventory.json`. This is a MEASURED span, not an estimate -- but it is an UPPER bound on any single cycle's true engineering time because it also carries queue/dispatch overhead between cycles (same caveat step-cost-ledger.derived.json already states).
measurement_method.units_cleared: for each commit, docs/work-inventory.json was checked out at that SHA (`git show <sha>:docs/work-inventory.json`) and partitioned with the live `completion_atlas.partition(units, book='core_rulebook')` function -- the same code the standing gate runs, not a re-implementation. Bucket deltas are the difference in bucket counts between consecutive commits.
measurement_method.bucket_attribution: each commit classified to a bucket by its own commit-message epic/bucket tag (AT-34-E3-001 -> B, AT-34-E3-002 -> C, AT-34-E3-003 'bucket U' -> U). Commits from Epic 1/Epic 2 (the rename, table-wiring) are reported separately as scaffolding, excluded from Epic 3's own totals.
measurement_method.redrive_command: git log --reverse --format='%H|%ct|%s' ea2b3396f2..HEAD -- docs/work-inventory.json for commits/timestamps; then per commit, git show <sha>:docs/work-inventory.json fed through completion_atlas.partition(json.load(fh)['units'], book='core_rulebook') for bucket counts. The full per-commit output is committed alongside this file as step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json -- every wall_min/bucket_delta figure above is aggregated from it.

B.meaning: table exists, record not in it (BUCKET_DEFINITIONS['B'])
B.closure_vs_reclassification: of the 503 units that LEFT bucket B, 235 reached DONE (real closure) and 268 moved to another unfinished bucket (D, V, X, or M) -- reclassification, not closure. Movement recorded per `decisions.md §12` L10: a count that drops because measurement changed is not closure.

dominant_mechanism.name: ground Favored Enemy/Favored Terrain display records off their sibling Bonus records

This is reclassification (A->B->C->V is forward movement) not closure.

headline_finding: Bucket B's per-mechanism spread (22 to 617 wall-minutes per cycle, a 28x range across 29 cycles) is the load-bearing number for Epic 5's pricing: a SINGLE blended 'units/hour' figure across bucket B would misrepresent every mechanism. The dominant driver by wall time is class_feature_option_pool_with_magnitude's cycle 8 (617.4 min, 2 units) -- a live domain-power probe requiring per-unit verification rather than a batch-groundable pattern; the cheapest driver is 'AT-34-E3-001 domain mechanism' (1 unit in 40.3 min) and 'merge: tranche/14' reconciliation (22.2 min, 3 units, batch pattern already proven). Bucket U is far cheaper per unit closed (40.28 units/hour) than bucket B (5.8 units/hour) because both U cycles were instrument corrections applying to a class of units at once, not per-record grounding.
